_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, docs, reference data, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data: rows that look like real records, whose real version is
sitting right there in the operator's life and is structurally indistinguishable.
Must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py -- a real record cannot be regenerated,
so pasting one in fails at commit. (A self-evidently fake canary or an Acme mock is
NOT lifelike and does not need a generator; the risk it guards against is a person
reaching for a convenient REAL example, and there is no temptation to reach for a
real value that would look obviously wrong next to FAKE_CANARY_XYZ.)
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never in a PUBLIC repo. Lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. This repo ships only the schema.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
`tool` is not a fourth class. It is the per-path allowlist for check 4, which fails any tracked
file that WEARS the shape of real-run output. TOOL is the default class and needs no entry --
except where a hand-written file is shaped like a ledger, which has to be argued for in the diff.
_tool_note: Hand-cut replay inputs for the signal-yield engine (test_yield.py, test_yield_temporal.py): 19 jsonl lines with ids op-a/op-b and a deliberately dead handle, plus the three-entry roster those runs replay against. They carry the LIVE LEDGER's filenames because the reader resolves an archive dir by name, so the test cannot exercise the real path under any other name -- which is exactly why they are enumerated rather than exempted by directory: the name stays usable for tests and unusable for a record. roster.json joined this list on 2026-08-27, when check 4 learned the roster shape; it was already tracked and already unclassified, and nothing had ever objected.
_fixture_note: 2026-08-27. tools/make_fixtures.py now exists, so `fixture` is a live class here rather than an empty list check 2 iterated zero times. It currently generates ONE file, and that file is the one that had actually gone wrong: tests/fixtures/watchlist.with-sources.json was a trimmed COPY OF THE OPERATOR'S LIVE PRIVATE WATCHLIST -- same source tuning, same subreddit picks, same CN feed publisher, and the operator's real daily cron, local timezone and quiet hours. It announced itself as a 'PARSE-ONLY TEST FIXTURE (not live config)' and that sentence was the whole control: perfectly true, and it stopped nothing, because the fixture's problem was never that someone might RUN it. It is now regenerated from the generator, with the person-shaped values drawn from the synthetic namespace (example.com, r/example-*, UTC) and a canary field naming the generator. The values the test suite genuinely pins (min_faves_rostered 25, community_pulse max_per_day 8 and its label, linux.do routes/fetch/category, v2ex fetch and its PUBLIC node slugs, the two disabled lanes) are kept and each is commented in the generator with the property that depends on it.
_fixture_backlog: NOT YET generator-backed, recorded here so the gap is a known number rather than a silence: the four parse fixtures under tests/fixtures/sources/ (x-get_user_info.json, x-get_user_last_tweets.json, v2ex-hot.json, linuxdo-latest.rss) and the three yield replay inputs listed under `tool` above. They are lifelike, so they belong in `fixture` eventually. They are not there yet for a reason that is about ownership, not about principle: their exact contents encode the scenarios that test_yield / test_yield_temporal / test_attribution assert on line by line, and folding them into the generator has to happen in the same change as any edit to those suites. The previous version of this note claimed the blocker was that no generator existed; that reason expired on 2026-08-27 and this one replaces it. Closing condition: move each path from `tool` to `fixture` and add a builder to tools/make_fixtures.py; check 2 then enforces byte-equality and the `tool` allowlist shrinks.
_audited: 2026-08-27 RE-AUDIT (supersedes 2026-07-31, which was accurate prose about a check that was not looking). What changed materially: (1) archive.resolve_archive_dir NO LONGER has a fallback. It used to end in `Path.home() / '.daily-hotspots-config' / 'archive'` and archive_card then mkdir'd it, so an uninitialized machine did not fail -- it conjured a companion config at a scattered $HOME path and started a real opportunity ledger inside it, with no remote, no history and no backup, and 'uninitialized' and 'initialized at the default' became the same observable state. It now raises ArchiveDirNotInitialized with an init hint. (2) The writers are wired to tools/datadir.py. Until now NO shipped writer imported it: archive.py and roster.py each had their own probe order, so the resolver every document in this fleet points at decided nothing and its guarantees protected no actual write. archive.py now resolves through it (roster.py is tracked separately, see _dependencies). (3) The explicit-arg hole named in the 2026-07-31 note -- 'the explicit-arg branch will hand back whatever a caller passes' -- is closed: --archive-dir now goes through datadir.assert_outside_own_repo, so both branches are covered by the same refusal. The `data` list stays EMPTY and that is still a finding, not a default: every byte of real-run output lands in the PRIVATE companion repo (archive/opportunities.jsonl, archive/pulls-YYYY-MM.jsonl, archive/dedup-state.json, archive/digests/YYYY/, roster.json, and a .run-YYYY-MM-DD/ scratch tree per run), which is the decided shape and not a problem. watchlist.json is a user INPUT read from the companion, not output.
_armed: 2026-08-27 RE-ARMED. Check 4's shape list was recalibrated against a REAL RUN, because it had never been. Measured before the change: the shipped RUN_SHAPES matched 0 of the 116 files one real daily run produces and 3 of the 40 files in the live archive. It had printed green every day of its life, and it would have kept printing green with the entire run tree pasted into this repo, because it named the shapes of the fleet's OTHER skills (metrics/*.jsonl, runs/, a handful of ledger names) and none of this one's. That is the failure mode this repo's own guard docstring names -- a checker that is handed nothing prints the same green as a checker that found nothing wrong -- reproduced inside the checker itself. After the change: 1640/1640 files across all 35 real run trees match, 39/40 archive files match (the miss is archive/.gitkeep, a directory placeholder, correctly not run output), and the 99 tracked files of this repo produce exactly the matches enumerated in `tool` and `fixture` above and no others. The negative control is tools/test_data_boundary.py, which poisons a scratch repo with each shape and asserts the nonzero exit; before it existed, this gate shipped as CI with nothing that could turn it red.
_companion:
THE COMPANION REPO'S OWN HYGIENE, decided 2026-08-27. The private companion repo had 35 .run-YYYY-MM-DD/ trees (1640 files, ~1.5 GB) sitting UNTRACKED AND UNIGNORED, against 40 tracked files. That limbo is the actual problem, not the tracking question: nothing backs those files up, and `git status` there was 1629 lines of noise, so a genuinely new file could not be seen. DECISION: IGNORE them. Verified first that nothing curated is lost -- every opportunity_id in every .run-*/opportunities*.jsonl (218 rows across two files) is already present in the tracked archive/opportunities.jsonl, and every dated markdown in the run trees has a tracked digest for its date; the trees hold raw third-party captures, fetch logs, stderr dumps and one-off scraper scripts, none of which the skill reads again. Tracking them would also put other people's raw scraped posts under permanent version control in every future clone and backup, which is a worse trade than losing scratch. THE OPERATOR RUNS, in the private companion repo (this public repo must not and does not do it): `printf '
# per-run scratch trees: raw captures, logs, one-off scripts. The curated record
# (archive/, roster.json) is tracked; these are not.
/.run-*/
' >> .gitignore` then `git add .gitignore && git commit -m 'ignore per-run scratch trees'`. Pruning old trees is a separate housekeeping choice and is not implied by the ignore rule. AUDIT IT, do not trust this paragraph: `python tools/data_boundary.py --companion` resolves the companion through datadir.py and exits 1 while shaped run output is loose, 0 when it is either tracked or ignored, and 3 when no companion resolves at all (nothing examined, which is not a clean bill of health).
_dependencies: roster.py's resolve_roster_path still carries the same two defects archive.py just lost (a `Path.home() / '.daily-hotspots-config' / 'roster.json'` fallback, and its own probe order instead of datadir.py). It is owned by another change in flight and is not touched here. The contract it should meet is archive.py's: resolve through tools/datadir.py, hard-fail on the write path with an init hint, and route any explicit path argument through datadir.assert_outside_own_repo. Also unwired: nothing in .github/workflows/ runs tools/test_data_boundary.py, so the negative control added on 2026-08-27 is not yet CI-enforced; it needs a step next to the existing tools/test_datadir.py one, and that step must NOT be wrapped in a file-existence test (see the note in that workflow about steps that fail open).
_data_home: The PRIVATE companion repo, resolved by tools/datadir.py: $DAILY_HOTSPOTS_CONFIG, else the sibling <parent>/daily-hotspots-config, else ~/.daily-hotspots-config, else ~/.config/daily-hotspots-config. If this skill needs to record real-run output, it goes THERE -- never back into this repo, and never at a scattered $HOME path invented at write time because nothing was configured.
